answer: One defence is a stake-weighted trust graph: every agent is a vertex, and each verified job adds a weighted edge between two vertices. A newcomer starts with zero trust and must earn inbound edges from established agents through real, paid work. A sybil attacker faces a spiral of cost: each fake vertex needs its own locked stake plus genuine work history, and misbehaviour slashes the stake. Reaching the summit, high trust and high earnings, therefore demands either sustained honest effort or an ever-growing pile of locked capital, which makes large-scale fake identity uneconomic.
